narrative.headline: Top 50 mega-caps tilt decisively bullish — 25 names BULLISH vs 14 BEARISH, with institutional accumulation concentrated in mega-cap tech and value names.

AAPL: $46M call premium paired with $1.43B dark pool accumulation, max blocks score
META: $22.7M call flow + $1.65B dark pool — mega-cap tech accumulation theme
ORCL: $26.3M call premium + $279M dark pool, blocks at 9.83 — software conviction extends beyond hyperscalers
INTC: $30.4M call flow + $273M dark pool — contrarian semis accumulation
AMAT: $4.8M call premium with $907M dark pool — semicap equipment buying
WMT/COST: perfect 10.0 composites — defensive consumer staples being aggressively accumulated
CSCO: $8.3M call flow + $395M dark pool, max blocks — networking re-rate
WFC/C/AXP: financials cluster bullish on strong flow scores (10.0/8.98/10.0)

LLY: flow 4.16 with max dark pool — distribution into size, weakest healthcare read
GS: flow 3.30 — bearish positioning diverges from bullish WFC/C/AXP financials cohort
PLTR: flow 3.41 — momentum name seeing put-side institutional hedging
CAT/GE: industrials weak (flow 4.03/1.67) despite heavy block activity
V: flow 1.78 — diverges sharply from bullish AXP, payments split
ABBV/PG: defensive healthcare/staples weak (flow 2.87/2.07) — selective within defensives
narrative.rotation_signal: Clear accumulation into mega-cap tech ex-MSFT (GOOGL, AAPL, META, ORCL), semis (AMAT, INTC, CSCO), money-center banks (WFC, C, AXP), and defensive retail (WMT, COST, HD). Distribution rotating out of MSFT, GS, LLY, PLTR, and old-economy industrials (CAT, GE) — a barbell of growth-tech + value-financials being funded by selling momentum and industrial cyclicals.
narrative.diverging_from_industry_layer: MSFT bearish read diverges sharply from broader software/AI bullishness seen in GOOGL/META/ORCL. GS bearish vs WFC/C/AXP bullish signals a money-center-over-investment-bank preference. V bearish vs AXP bullish splits the payments complex. LLY/ABBV weakness contrasts with JNJ bullish (9.60) — pharma is being picked, not bought as a sector.
